topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines learning objectives, and sets the clinical and biological framing for cancer biology.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer as a disruption of cellular genetics and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biological basis of cancer as a progressive failure of cellular differentiation, genetic regulation, and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Pathology and progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained, benign precursor lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies, highlighting histological evidence and the adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and clinical mechanisms of morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail tumor classification conventions and the pathophysiological mechanisms through which both benign and malignant growths cause clinical harm and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the epidemiological patterns of cancer in humans and compare tumor occurrence across diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical applications of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate screening methods across different organ systems.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by reviewing learning outcomes and giving practical session announcements.
